newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-EDBERG MAKES FAREWELL APPEARANCE IN STOCKHOLM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-EDBERG MAKES FAREWELL APPEARANCE IN STOCKHOLM.

text.p: Former world number one Stefan Edberg will be the centre of attention at the Stockholm Open this week as he plays his final singles tournament before retiring from the international circuit.
The 30-year-old Swede is bound to receive an emotional farewell from his home crowd as he bows out after a 14-year career that brought him six Grand Slam titles.
"A lot of people are coming just to see him play for the last time," Stockholm Open official, Bodil Norrstrom, said on Monday.
Norrstrom said about 40,000 people were expected to attend the Stockholm Open that starts at the Royal Tennis Club in central Stockholm on Monday with the final on Sunday.
Edberg, the sixth seed, will launch his final singles campaign against fellow Swede Nicklas Kulti on Tuesday.

Although this is Edberg's farewell individual tournament before he bows out to spend more time with his family, he is expected to be chosen for the Swedish team in the Davis Cup final against France in Malmo, southern Sweden, in late November.
As Edberg prepares to leave the court for the last time, Sweden's media were already hailing 22-year-old Thomas Enqvist his successor.
Enqvist, Sweden's current number one, won the Paris Open on Sunday in straight sets against Russia's Yevgeny Kafelnikov, the French Open champion.
"Enqvist has hit his perfect form," said the Swedish tabloid newspaper Aftonbladet on Monday.
The Expressen newspaper said: "Stefan Edberg can bow out in peace. Thomas Enqvist has already taken over."
Enqvist, the third seed in the Stockholm Open that offers a top prize of 728,000 crowns ($111,000), is drawn in the first round against Australia's Richard Fromberg.
Edberg, who has always shunned the spotlight, made an emotional exit from competitive tennis outside Sweden when he was beaten 6-4 7-6 by Enqvist at the Paris Open last Friday.
He was presented with a miniature replica of the Paris Open trophy he won in 1990 and was given a standing ovation by the fans.
Edberg was due on Monday to award the first prizes from his newly-formed Stefan Edberg Foundation, set up this year to sponsor young, aspiring tennis players.
He himself was "discovered" at the age of 13 by Swedish trainer Percy Rosberg who also coached Bjorn Borg in the 1970s and 1980s.

Since Edberg's first big win in Milan in 1984, he has collected an estimated $20.7 million in prize money which he has invested in business and property. Only Pete Sampras and Ivan Lendl have earned more.
In 54 Grand Slam tournaments, Edberg has twice won the Wimbledon, U.S. Open and Australian Open titles. He has on the Davis Cup winning team three times, in 1984, 1985 and 1994.
Edberg, who has lived in Britain since 1984, has said he wants to spend more time with his wife, Annette and three-year-old daughter Emilie.
